messages:
Anya (Support): heads up — AcmeRetail escalated. They saw a huge billing spike + a ton of 429s during our internal throughput sweep this morning. They say their integration started failing and tokens were getting revoked. stack: hosted API, api-key auth, per-key quotas.

Maya (Support): copying the customer note: 'between 09:17–09:38 we had repeated 429s, latency spiked to 2.3s p95, and our invoice jumped ~15% from retries. We weren't doing anything different.' They attached some logs — dropped them into the ticket.

sre-bot: ALERT: loadtest-control-plane detected spike on /v1/generate from project: redwood-internal-loadtests at 2026-03-14T09:18:07Z — 10k RPM sustained for ~3m. 429 rate = 18%.

Raj (Eng-SRE): probable root causes to check: (1) per-key/token bucket exhausted due to long-running continuous load + retries, (2) our billing meter counting each attempt instead of successful tokens, (3) our auth layer is aggressively revoking stale tokens when rate-limit errors happen on backend.

Anya (Support): customer reports they were hit because our internal test used their API key as part of a managed demo; our test harness didn't isolate demo keys properly. Need repro steps + quick mitigation for customer.

Olivia (DevEx): Oof. Two things: immediate mitigation (for customer) — rotate the leaked key and issue a short credit refund; operational mitigation — make sure loadtests exclude customer keys and add a safety net on our end to cap outgoing per-key RPM from internal harnesses.

Leo (Eng-Infra): I'll take the internal harness change. Also need to reproduce locally to tune sane defaults for RPM/TPM and burst handling. Proposed repro plan: run a 3-phase k6 profile (warmup, ramp, steady) against a sandbox org key and observe: 95th latency, 429 rate, dropped requests per-second.

Maya (Support): can you paste the k6 script and exact command? Ops wants to run this against staging.

Raj (Eng-SRE): here's a minimal k6 flow to reproduce the behaviour we saw (paste into loadtests/investigations/acme-repro.js):

```js
import http from 'k6/http';
import { sleep } from 'k6';

export let options = {
  vus: 400,
  duration: '8m',
  stages: [
    { duration: '1m', target: 50 }, // warmup
    { duration: '2m', target: 400 }, // ramp to target
    { duration: '5m', target: 400 } // steady
  ],
  thresholds: {
    http_req_duration: ['p95<800'],
  },
};

export default function () {
  let res = http.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', JSON.stringify({ prompt: 'ping' }), {
    headers: { 'Authorization': 'Bearer $SANDBOX_KEY', 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
  });
  // no retries in this repro to show raw 429s
  sleep(0.3);
}
```

Run command: `k6 run -e SANDBOX_KEY=<staging-key> loadtests/investigations/acme-repro.js`

Raj (Eng-SRE): also test with a retrying client (exponential backoff + immediate retry) since retries were inflating billing. Example repro with vegeta or hey will show repeated attempts counted by meter.

Maya (Support): pasted a snippet from customer logs (redacted):

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rw-quota: user=120/300RPM; window=60s
x-rw-burst: 900/1200; burst-window=30s
message: rate limit exceeded
```

Anya (Support): They got billed for the retry attempts. Is billing currently counting attempts or only accepted tokens?

billing-bot: BILLING-TRACE: meter.v1.post_request logged 1 attempt per HTTP request; charge applied on request completion unless request returned 4xx/5xx with error_tag=non_billable. 429 currently not excluded.

Olivia (DevEx): that's a policy decision — but to avoid customer harm we should stop billing for 429/401 attempts for now and only bill on 2xx/3xx. Ops: can we patch this via config flag?

ops: we can flip a billing filter flag at the charge pipeline to exclude 429s immediately. Will require a rollback plan if we change accounting.

Leo (Eng-Infra): For defaults: our internal testing suggests these starting points (unique from prior threads):
- per-API-key soft RPM: 400 RPM (sustained), with a short-term burst allowance: 1400 requests over a 20s burst window (to allow spikes from small clients).
- per-account TPM (tokens per minute): 20k TPM capped.
- burst recovery/refill: leaky-bucket with refill-rate = 1 token per (60/400) seconds per key and a max-burst multiplier = 3.5x sustained rate.
- automatic backoff policy when 429% > 5%: reduce client allowance by 30% for 60s and notify owner via webhooks.

These are starting points — we need empirical confirmation.

Raj (Eng-SRE): experiment matrix to validate defaults:
- Sweep sustained RPMs [100, 200, 400, 800] across 4 runs.
- For each RPM, test burst windows [10s, 20s, 60s] with burst multipliers [2x, 3x, 5x].
- Measure p50/p95 latency, 429 rate, and billing events (attempts vs accepted).

Olivia (DevEx): measurement rules: 3 runs per combination, 90% confidence intervals. Evaluate: acceptable 429 <= 1% and p95 < 800ms under steady state. Anything outside triggers tuning.

Anya (Support): for immediate customer remediation: 1) rotate their compromised key, 2) issue credit equal to attempts billed during the window, 3) explain mitigation steps and ETA. I've drafted a short message.

Maya (Support): customer-facing snippet added to ticket: "we found our internal test used a key in a demo flow. We're rotating keys and applying a credit. We're also updating our internal harness to never run against customer-owned keys and will hard-cap internal test traffic per key." 

Raj (Eng-SRE): infra TODOs:
- [ ] add a safety cap on internal-loadtest orchestrator: no more than 50 RPM per external key by default and block non-sandbox keys. (Leo)
- [ ] patch billing pipeline to exclude 429 attempts pending policy review. (ops)
- [ ] run the full experiment matrix in staging and collect metrics. (Olivia + Raj)
- [ ] create a dashboard to show attempts vs accepted (billing delta) per key. (Leo)

Leo (Eng-Infra): I'll push a canary of the leaky-bucket config to staging with the 400RPM/1400burst initial values and run the matrix. Will report results by EOD tomorrow.

Olivia (DevEx): one more thought — default client SDKs should implement jittered exponential backoff and caps on retries (max 3). We should add README guidance on retries so partners don't accidentally amplify load.

Anya (Support): closing loop items for support: issue credit, rotate key, notify customer of fix and timeline. I've scheduled a short postmortem channel invite for Monday.

sre-bot: TASK CREATED: loadtest-matrix-1836543210 assigned to Raj, Leo, Olivia — due 2026-03-15T23:59:00Z.

Maya (Support): thanks team. I'll update the ticket with the remediation steps and link to this thread. If staging repro shows different 429 patterns we'll iterate on the burst window numbers.

Raj (Eng-SRE): final note — when we run the matrix, capture client-side retry behavior telemetry; it's the biggest wildcard for billing/inflation. If clients retry immediately, burst handling needs to be much more conservative.

Anya (Support): agreed. tagging @ops for the billing filter flip, @leo for canary, and @olivia for experiment orchestration.

[thread ends]
